questions.question: What is the fundamental period of the function f(t) = sin(2πt) + cos(4πt)?
questions.tutor: Period of sin(2πt) is 1, cos(4πt) period is 1/2. Fundamental period = LCM = 1.

questions.question: In Fourier series, the constant term a₀/2 represents:
questions.tutor: a₀/2 = (1/T)∫f(t)dt, the DC or average value over one period.

questions.question: What is the Maclaurin series of cos x?
questions.tutor: cos x = Σ (-1)ⁿ x²ⁿ/(2n)!.

questions.question: Find the Fourier coefficient a₁ for f(x)=x on [-π,π].
questions.tutor: a_n = (1/π)∫_{-π}^{π} x cos(nx) dx. For odd function, all a_n = 0.

questions.question: What is the radius of convergence of Σ (x-1)ⁿ / n²?
questions.tutor: Ratio test: |a_{n+1}/a_n| = n²/(n+1)² → 1, so R=1.

questions.question: For a Fourier series of a square wave, which harmonics are present?
questions.tutor: Square wave has half-wave symmetry → only odd harmonics (1,3,5,...).

questions.question: What is the Taylor series of ln(1+x) about x=0?
What does the Fourier series converge to at a jump discontinuity?
choices: Average of left and right limits
questions.tutor: Fourier series converges to [f(t⁻)+f(t⁺)]/2 at a jump.

questions.question: Find the interval of convergence for Σ (3x)ⁿ.
questions.tutor: Geometric series converges when |3x|<1 → |x|<1/3.

questions.question: What is the Fourier series of an even function?
questions.tutor: Even functions have b_n = 0, only cosine terms.

questions.question: What is the power series expansion of e^{-x²} up to x⁴ term?
For f(t)=|t| on [-π,π], what type of Fourier series?
questions.tutor: |t| is even → only cosine terms.

questions.question: What is the radius of convergence of Σ n! xⁿ?
questions.tutor: Ratio test: lim |(n+1)!x^{n+1}/(n!xⁿ)| = lim (n+1)|x| = ∞ unless x=0 → R=0.

questions.question: What is the fundamental frequency of a signal with period T?
questions.tutor: Fundamental frequency f₀ = 1/T (Hz) or ω₀ = 2π/T (rad/s).

questions.question: Find the sum of the series Σ_{n=0}^∞ (-1)ⁿ/2ⁿ.
Parseval's theorem relates:
choices: Power in time domain to power in frequency domain
questions.tutor: Parseval: (1/T)∫|f(t)|² dt = Σ |c_n|², equating power.

questions.question: What is the Maclaurin series of sinh x?
For an odd function, Fourier coefficients:
questions.tutor: Odd functions have a₀=0 and all a_n=0; only sine terms remain.

questions.question: What is the Taylor polynomial of degree 2 for √(1+x) about x=0?
What is the Fourier series coefficient c₀ for f(t)=sin²(πt)?
questions.tutor: sin²(πt) = 1/2 - (1/2)cos(2πt) → average value = 1/2 = c₀.

questions.question: The series Σ xⁿ/n converges for:
questions.tutor: R=1 from ratio test. At x=1: harmonic series diverges. At x=-1: alternating harmonic series converges → |x|<1.

questions.question: What is the Fourier series of a sawtooth wave?
questions.tutor: Sawtooth (odd extension) has only sine terms.

questions.question: If f(x) = 1/(1-x), what is its Maclaurin series?
questions.tutor: 1/(1-x) = Σ xⁿ for |x|<1.

questions.question: Which function has a Fourier series with only even harmonics?
questions.tutor: Half-wave symmetry (f(t+T/2)=-f(t)) yields only odd harmonics, not even. Wait — half-wave gives odd. Even harmonics appear in certain rectified waves. Better: Full-wave rectified sine has only even harmonics.

questions.question: What is the sum of the series 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7 + ...?
questions.tutor: arctan x = x - x³/3 + x⁵/5 - ... At x=1: arctan 1 = π/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - ...

questions.question: The Gibbs phenomenon occurs:
questions.tutor: Gibbs overshoot (~9%) occurs near jump discontinuities in Fourier series.

questions.question: Find the Fourier series coefficient b₁ for f(x)=x on [-π,π].
questions.tutor: b_n = (1/π)∫_{-π}^{π} x sin(nx) dx. For n=1, b₁=2.

questions.question: What is the power series of arctan x?
questions.tutor: arctan x = Σ (-1)ⁿ x^{2n+1}/(2n+1).

questions.question: Complex Fourier series uses:
questions.tutor: Complex Fourier series uses c_n e^{jnω₀t} basis functions.

questions.question: What is the radius of convergence of Σ xⁿ / n²?
questions.tutor: lim |n²/(n+1)²| = 1 → R=1. Converges at endpoints also.
